Record date: 2129-06-26
South Elizabeth Seychelles Hospital INTERNAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT Location: 4923 Olivia Parkway Suite 217, Lake Jennabury
PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 80 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 06/26/29 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Persistent shortness of breath, worsening cough with increased sputum production, and significant fatigue.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax returns for follow-up approximately three weeks after his last visit. He reports that his shortness of breath has continued to escalate, now occurring at rest and severely limiting his ability to perform daily activities. He describes his reliance on his albuterol inhaler as excessive, using it up to thirty times a day, indicating a concerning exacerbation of his underlying pulmonary condition. His cough has intensified, with an increase in purulent sputum production, which remains greenish and now frequently contains blood. These symptoms raise the suspicion for a possible exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) or an acute infectious process such as pneumonia.
Additionally, Mr. Fairfax expresses concern regarding his persistent fatigue, which has become debilitating. He notes that he experiences significant bilateral lower extremity edema, which has progressed to involve his thighs, and he describes the swelling as painful and uncomfortable. His insomnia remains a significant issue, with anxiety related to his respiratory symptoms contributing to his poor sleep quality. He reports averaging only 1-2 hours of sleep per night despite trying various over-the-counter sleep aids without success.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + fatigue, + weight gain, no fevers or chills. Pulmonary - + persistent shortness of breath at rest, + worsening cough with greenish and blood-tinged sputum, - hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain or palpitations, + orthopnea, - paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - + joint pain, + severe bilateral lower extremity edema. Neurological - no dizziness or headaches.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: - Blood Pressure: 150/90 mmHg - Heart Rate: 92 bpm - Respiratory Rate: 24 breaths/min - Oxygen Saturation: 88% on room air
General: The patient appears in moderate respiratory distress, using accessory muscles for breathing.
HEENT: No nasal flaring, oropharynx clear.
Lungs: Diminished breath sounds bilaterally with wheezing noted on expiration; crackles heard on auscultation of the lower lung fields.
Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs or gallops.
Extremities: Marked bilateral lower extremity edema, extending to the thighs, with pitting noted.
ASSESSMENT
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease exacerbation, likely multifactorial including possible infection. 2. Congestive heart failure, exacerbated by fluid overload. 3. Insomnia secondary to anxiety and respiratory distress.
PLAN
1. Initiate a course of oral corticosteroids (prednisone 40 mg daily for 5 days) to reduce airway inflammation. 2. Start a course of antibiotics (azithromycin 500 mg daily for 5 days) to address potential bacterial infection. 3. Increase the frequency of nebulized albuterol treatments to every 4 hours as needed, and consider adding ipratropium bromide for further bronchodilation. 4. Recommend diuretics (furosemide 40 mg daily) to manage fluid overload and reduce edema. 5. Schedule a follow-up appointment in one week to reassess respiratory status and adjust treatment as necessary. 6. Discussed the importance of smoking cessation and provided resources for cessation programs. 7. Addressed sleep issues, recommending cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) and a referral to a sleep specialist if symptoms persist.
The patient was educated on the new medications, potential side effects, and the importance of adherence to the treatment plan. He verbalized understanding and agreed to the proposed management strategy.
DISPOSITION
Mr. Fairfax was stable for discharge with a follow-up appointment scheduled for 07/03/29. He was advised to seek immediate medical attention if he experiences worsening shortness of breath, chest pain, or any new concerning symptoms.
